class.name: FSPropertyDescriptor
class.brief_description: A read-only structured descriptor for a single reflected [FoundryScript] member variable.
class.description: Describes one member variable declared by a [FoundryScript] type or its base scripts, as a typed alternative to the loosely-keyed [Dictionary] entries of [method FSReflection.get_properties]. Instances are produced by [method FSReflection.get_property_descriptors] and are immutable snapshots of the compiled property metadata. Beyond the [method Object.get_property_list] fields it mirrors ([member name], [member type], [member class_name], [member hint], [member hint_string], and [member usage]), each descriptor carries the variable's passive [member annotations] and its exact declared [member type_name]. The accessors return copies, so mutating them does not change the script's stored metadata. Use [method to_dictionary] to obtain the equivalent loosely-keyed descriptor [Dictionary].

method.name: to_dictionary
method.description: Returns the equivalent loosely-keyed property descriptor [Dictionary], matching the entries of [method FSReflection.get_properties]: an [method Object.get_property_list] [Dictionary] plus [code]"annotations"[/code] and [code]"type_name"[/code] keys holding the [member annotations] and [member type_name].

members.member: The passive annotations applied to the member variable, in source order, as [FSAnnotation] descriptors. Empty when the variable has no annotations. Each call returns an independent snapshot.
The property's class name, as in an [method Object.get_property_list] entry. Empty unless the property's type carries a class.
The property's hint, one of the [enum PropertyHint] values.
The property's hint string, paired with [member hint].

The exact FoundryScript type the variable was declared with, for example [code]"ulong"[/code], [code]"Array[int]"[/code], or [code]"Dictionary[uint, long]"[/code]. Unlike [member type], which carries only the [enum Variant.Type] the value travels in, this keeps the declared integer width and the element, key, and value types of a typed container, so [code]Array[int][/code] and [code]Array[long][/code] stay distinguishable. The name comes from the compiled declaration, never from a stored value. Empty for a native property, which has no FoundryScript declaration to name. An integer slot that declares no width names the full range its carrier spans ([code]"long"[/code] or [code]"ulong"[/code]), since narrowing it further would claim a constraint the declaration never had.
The property's usage flags, a bitmask of [enum PropertyUsageFlags] values.
